source_books: The Dark Eye 4th Edition — Armor (Fandom wiki: tde4e.fandom.com/wiki/Armor and linked armor articles)
meta.notes: AR/RS = armor rating; EC/BE = encumbrance. Weights in stones (Stein, 1 Stein ≈ 1 kg per wiki). Prices in silver thalers (S). Values +X on wiki helmets/additional pieces stored as positive AR/EC. Combining/stacking, torso-only exceptions, and metal-magic rules per wiki. Mass-produced / masterwork / loot modifiers omitted here. Toadshide & Strip Apron: wiki assigns effective metallic EC 1 for spell penalties.

armor.name: Padded Tunic
armor.description: This consists of two layers of coarse linen or other fabric quilted to form tubes, pockets, or panels that are stuffed with horsehair or seagrass. It is ideal under a cuirass or light plate (in which case the AR and EC add up), but it is also useful on its own, as the padded tunic (also called a gambeson) absorbs the blunt force of a blow.
armor.special: Gambeson-style padded coat; stacks with allowed torso armor per wiki combining rules.

armor.name: Padded Underclothes
armor.description: This is needed under all metal armor (chain, plate) to prevent chafing and pressure points. It consists of two-layered, coarse linen leggings, a tunic, gloves, and a coif. The AR and EC of the undergarments do not add to the value of the armor worn over it; the values given apply if the padded clothing is worn on its own. Some forms of padded undergarments, designed specifically for use under plate armor, have reinforcements made of chain pieces in the areas that are usually left exposed by the plate armor.
armor.special: Under-layer; undergarment AR/EC typically do not add when worn beneath metal armor that requires them (wiki).

armor.name: Thick Clothes
armor.description: As a complete set (shirt, pants, jacket, shoes), this includes all forms of winter or related fur clothing, full-leather wilderness clothing, heavy leather jerkins worn over street clothes, barbaric-looking fur coats, heavy coachmen coats, and even certain brocade and velvet festive garments, specifically those that are heavily lined. Normal street clothes, and even more so loincloths and thin silk clothing, count as AR 0 and bring no hindrance. The AR of thick clothing does not add to the value of any armor worn over it, but it can replace the undergarments. Thick clothing can also be supplemented by a helmet.
armor.special: Heavy everyday clothing; price varies by garment (placeholder cost).

armor.name: Breastplate
armor.description: This is usually a round hard leather plate held on the chest by leather straps. It is popular in similar forms among all tribal cultures and with gladiators. It can be combined with normal clothing. Metal versions are simply a bit thinner for the same weight and protective effect.
armor.special: Strapped breastplate; wiki lists as non-forged-metal exception for magic interaction.

armor.name: Iryan Armor
armor.description: This is a decorative and expensive armor made from the fireproofed leather of southern Aventurian swamp lizards. It is often dyed in bright colors. For the same resistance, it is slightly thinner and more mobile than ordinary leather armor and is therefore about one and a half times as expensive.
armor.special: Regional leather armor style.

armor.name: Leather Cuirass
armor.description: This is hard leather armor, made by boiling multiple layers of sewn leather in hot wax (which is why it is also called boiled leather or Kurbul). It is usually in the shape of a human torso with additional shoulder reinforcement, making it a widespread armor because it is relatively light, robust, and inexpensive.
armor.special: Hardened leather torso and arms.

armor.name: Toadshide
armor.description: This is a vest of thick leather with heavy rivets, popular among the Thorwalians.
armor.special: Thick leather with rivets; wiki: count metallic EC 1 for spell-hindrance rules.

armor.name: Chain Mail Vest
armor.description: A tightly woven mesh of wire rings that offers good protection and is easy to wear, but is also quite heavy. The chain mail vest is sleeveless and covers only the torso. It can be combined with thick clothing, otherwise requires only normal clothing as undergarments.
armor.special: Short mail torso.

armor.name: Chain Mail Shirt
armor.description: A tightly woven mesh of wire rings that offers good protection and is easy to wear, but is also quite heavy. The ordinary (short) chain mail shirt has sleeves to the elbow. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Standard mail shirt.

armor.name: Chain Mail Shirt, Long
armor.description: A tightly woven mesh of wire rings that offers good protection and is easy to wear, but is also quite heavy. The long-sleeved and thigh-length chain mail shirt of traditional knights. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Long mail covering thighs.

armor.name: Chain Mail Coat
armor.description: A tightly woven mesh of wire rings that offers good protection and is easy to wear, but is also quite heavy. Calf-length chain coats that are slitted at the front and back to allow for riding. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Full-length mail coat.

armor.name: Iron Coat
armor.description: In brigandine style, metal plates are riveted onto fabric or leather so that you only see the rivets from the outside, and the inside is covered with another layer of fabric. For especially robust examples, another layer of fabric and metal is added. The iron coat is a knee-length coat in three-layer brigandine, popular with merchants and shady characters because of its harmless appearance.
armor.special: Heavy reinforced mail variant.

armor.name: Mirror Mail
armor.description: A typical armor of Tulamydian potentates: a fine chain mail mesh with integrated or attached plate pieces. It is usually richly decorated. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Polished reflective mail; wiki price 1000+ S.

armor.name: Layered Armor
armor.description: In brigandine style, metal plates are riveted onto fabric or leather so that you only see the rivets from the outside, and the inside is covered with another layer of fabric. For especially robust examples, another layer of fabric and metal is added. Layered armor is thicker than the iron coat, but only protects the torso and thighs.
armor.special: Layered construction (regional).

armor.name: Ring Mail
armor.description: Metal rings, usually interwoven, are sewn onto soft leather. It is lighter and more mobile than the Middenrealm chain mail shirt. This armor comes with long sleeves and is from the Tulamydian regions.
armor.special: Rings sewn to backing.

armor.name: Scale Mail
armor.description: This armor consists of leather with sewn-on, and often riveted, bronze scales, and is lined with felt on the inside. It is now a rare and very expensive traditional armor from northwestern Aventuria.
armor.special: Overlapping scales.

armor.name: Bronze Cuirass
armor.description: This is an ancient torso armor made of bronze, padded with felt on the inside. Similar in form to a leather cuirass, it is often combined with a strip apron but is now almost exclusively used as parade armor and by gladiators.
armor.special: Bronze torso plate.

armor.name: Cuirass
armor.description: A roughly anatomically shaped breastplate of solid steel, it is held in place on the back by crisscrossing leather straps. It is popular among light cavalry and foot soldiers. It can be combined with thick clothing and otherwise only requires normal clothing as undergarments.
armor.special: Steel breast and back.

armor.name: Garethian Plate
armor.description: A heavy yet mobile foot soldier armor that protects the body from the base of the neck to the knees and fingertips. It is made entirely of articulated plate pieces and is typically combined with a sallet. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Full Garethian plate harness; wiki price 750+ S.

armor.name: Gladiator Shoulder
armor.description: A wide, ornate, articulated (and therefore very mobile) protection for the left shoulder, upper arm, and elbow of gladiators; held in position by leather straps that also provide a little protection for the left rib cage. It is made from either an ornate leather/bronze combination or steel, which makes no difference in weight or protective effect; the archaic type is simply more expensive. The variant for women also includes breast cups; a combination of a gladiator shoulder and breast cups is therefore not possible, nor is the combination of two gladiator shoulders.
armor.special: Partial shoulder/arm protection; combining limits per wiki.

armor.name: Kuslik Lamellar
armor.description: This is an outdated traditional armor of the Old Empire, now only used for parades. It consists of overlapping metal strips on leather carrying straps. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Laced lamellar plates (Kuslik style).

armor.name: Light Plate
armor.description: This armor features a steel chest and back plate (with the chest and back each consisting of two interlocking pieces for better mobility) with lamellar skirts for the thighs. It is a popular choice for cavalry and pikemen. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Can be worn over padded tunic with fit adjustments (wiki combining notes).

armor.name: Maraskan Hardwood Cuirass
armor.description: This armor consists of overlapping plates of a very light hardwood. It is sensitive to moisture, so it is often painted in bright colors (both for this reason and to ward off various Maraskan venomous creatures). It usually provides torso protection with shoulder, upper arm, and thigh pieces of the same style. Since the occupation of Maraskan by the Borbaradians, it is now rare and very expensive. The armor must be regularly maintained (daily in humid conditions), otherwise it will begin to rot and lose its stability. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Laminated hardwood; non-metal for wiki magic list.

armor.name: Mammoth Hide Armor
armor.description: This is an extremely rare body armor from Northern Aventuria, attributed to the elves. Round scales made of magically treated (or so it is said) mammoth ivory are sewn onto a layer of tough yet flexible leather. This armor is not available on the open market, not even in Northern Aventuria.
armor.special: Rare hide construction.

armor.name: Amazon Armor
armor.description: Amazons traditionally wear a fixed armor combination that also serves as their uniform. This includes a shoulderless, form-fitting bronze cuirass, as well as forearm and lower leg splints of hardened and reinforced leather, and a leather strip apron. A visorless helmet with a horsehair plume completes the armor. Female officers wear a helmet ornament of ostrich feathers.
armor.special: Full set; not normally sold (wiki).

armor.name: Horasian Rider Armor
armor.description: The plate armor of the Horasian cavalry consists of an articulated chest and back plate with long leg protection, neck, shoulder, and arm armor, gauntlets, and a visorless helmet. The entire set is intended to blend seamlessly and cannot be combined with any other armor pieces. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Cavalry full harness; wiki price 1000+ S.

armor.name: Jousting Armor
armor.description: This type of armor is intended for riders, and in this case, specifically for tournament riders. Consequently, this armor is custom-made and usually decorated with engravings, punchwork, inlays, and the like—it is sports equipment and a showpiece for those who can afford it. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Tournament plate; extremely encumbering; wiki price 2500+ S. Full sets cannot combine with other armor (wiki).

armor.name: Baburian Hat
armor.description: A leather helmet reinforced with metal bits and featuring a long neck guard of chain mail strips. This type of helmet is popular throughout the entire Tulamydian area.
armor.special: Additive head AR/EC; benefits require sufficient torso AR per wiki (+helmet needs torso AR ≥2).

armor.name: Chain Mail Cap
armor.description: A close-fitting coif of chain mail mesh with shoulder protection. It requires appropriate undergarments and is often worn in combination with a great helm. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Coif; combines only with certain outer helmets per wiki.

armor.name: Great Helmet
armor.description: A massive, often visorless, iron helmet of a roughly cylindrical shape and often a flat top. Requires undergarments.
armor.special: Heavy pot helm; vision/perception penalties at GM discretion (rulebook).

armor.name: Iron Cap
armor.description: A cap made of metal and sporting a broad rim; it is popular with demolition soldiers.
armor.special: Light metal skull cap.

armor.name: Leather Helmet
armor.description: Usually just a skullcap of hardened boiled leather, lined with a layer of felt. The reinforced variant has additional edge and seam reinforcements made of more leather or metal strips.
armor.special: Can stack with chain coif per wiki head-combining rules.

armor.name: Morion
armor.description: A helmet type common in the Horasian Empire with a brim that is raised at the front and back.
armor.special: High-comb infantry helm.

armor.name: Sounder
armor.description: A Garethian helmet type with a wide, flared neck guard and often a movable visor. It is worn together with a steel beard—a full metal collar that protects the neck and the lower part of the face.
armor.special: Includes face protection (beard/bevor); wiki name Sounder.

armor.name: Storm Cap
armor.description: A tight-fitting iron helmet without a brim, popular with mercenaries.
armor.special: Reinforced cap style.

armor.name: Leather Greaves
armor.description: Forearm, lower leg, and if necessary neck and shoulder protection made of hardened or heavy leather, additionally also occasionally gloves and footwear. The armor values apply to a complete set of gear—meaning at least one pair of the respective arm and leg protectors. To benefit from leather greaves, a fighter needs a torso AR of 3 or more.
armor.special: Additive leg AR; effective vs called shots only if torso AR high enough (wiki: greaves need torso AR ≥3).

armor.name: Chain Mail Greaves
armor.description: Forearm, lower leg, and if necessary neck and shoulder protection made of interlocking metal rings, additionally also occasionally gloves and footwear. The armor values apply to a complete set of gear—meaning at least one pair of the respective arm and leg protectors. To benefit from chain mail greaves, a fighter needs a torso AR of 4 or more.
armor.special: Wiki notes high weight; requires torso AR ≥4 to matter on legs in abstract combat.

armor.name: Plate Greaves
armor.description: Forearm, lower leg, and if necessary neck and shoulder protection made of solid metal plates, additionally also occasionally gloves and footwear. The armor values apply to a complete set of gear—meaning at least one pair of the respective arm and leg protectors. To benefit from plate greaves, a fighter needs a torso AR of 4 or more.
armor.special: Plate leg harness pieces; torso AR ≥4 for benefit vs leg hits (wiki).

armor.name: Strip Apron
armor.description: This is a typical gladiator armor that can only be combined with armor pieces (such as a chain mail vest, gladiator shoulder, or bronze cuirass) that do not already protect the groin area. It is usually an apron reinforced with rivets or plate pieces, made of overlapping leather strips that are about knee-length and held in place by a hand-width, metal-fitted belt. Similar armor pieces made of thick fur are also known from the Fjarninger and Trollzacker, and a strip apron also belongs as a single piece to Amazon armor.
armor.special: Leather strip protection; wiki: count metallic EC 1 for spell hindrance.
